skill.name: set-up-shopify-meta-ltv-bidding
skill.description: Set up Meta lifetime value bidding for Shopify with Product Metrics. Check server-side tracking, then validate revenue or profit signals from paid orders.
skill.summary: Guide Meta Ads setup for observed Shopify customer lifetime revenue or profit.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most static matches were documentation or routine setup operations, with no evidence of host reconnaissance, credential exfiltration, or prompt injection. The unpinned installer and authenticated remote MCP fallback introduce trust risks. The workflow also accepts tokens through the assistant, puts consent review after destination setup, and gives conflicting advice for profit LTV.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer version and skill revision to reviewed releases. Require user approval before running the installer.

remediation.issue: Authenticated remote MCP operations lack an explicit trust check
remediation.suggestion: Verify the MCP server, use least-privilege credentials, and allowlist documented operations. Confirm the account, destination, and intended changes before each authenticated write.

remediation.issue: Meta access tokens can enter assistant and tool transcripts
remediation.suggestion: Remove the assistant credential exception. Require token entry in the Product Metrics app or a verified secret-entry flow that keeps tokens out of model inputs and command arguments.
Verify the selected banner and LTV consent requirements before enabling delivery. Confirm that an order without the required consent produces no Meta LTV event.

remediation.issue: Profit LTV handoff names a conflicting optimization event
remediation.suggestion: Use PMProfitLTV with CUSTOMER_PROFIT_LTV for lifetime profit. Label PMOrderProfit as order-profit bidding and verify the test event and ad set selection before launch.

semantic_findings.title: Assistant is told to collect a Meta access token
semantic_findings.description: The skill allows the assistant to request the token and pass it to a command. Hiding it from summaries does not protect it from chat history, tool traces, or process inspection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both passages explicitly permit assistant receipt of the token. Neither describes a secret-entry channel that keeps it out of the conversation and tool arguments.

semantic_findings.title: Meta delivery is enabled before consent is checked
semantic_findings.description: The connection guide leaves sending on, and the LTV guide says sending starts after connection. The LTV workflow verifies the consent banner only afterward, leaving existing consent settings unchecked at activation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented sequence enables delivery before verifying consent. There is no evidence that Product Metrics actually sends events when consent is absent.

semantic_findings.title: Profit LTV guidance can select the wrong bidding signal
semantic_findings.description: The main instructions recommend the order-profit event for profit bidding, but the LTV reference uses a separate profit LTV event. Following the main instructions can optimize ad spend for order profit instead of lifetime profit.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The two guides name different events and purpose filters for the profit goal. The merchant makes the final selection, so incorrect optimization is possible but not automatic.

content.user_title: Set Up Shopify Lifetime Value Bidding in Meta
content.value_statement: A first order can understate the value of customers who buy again. Use Product Metrics to verify Shopify lifetime value signals and choose the matching Meta conversion.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status and identify which Shopify and Meta setup steps remain.
Guide the merchant through connecting Shopify and a Meta pixel or dataset for server-side tracking.
Check whether a Shopify test order is associated with a recognized customer.
Explain the consent and cost requirements for revenue and profit LTV events.
Guide creation of the matching Meta custom conversion and verify test event delivery.
limitations: Requires a Product Metrics Shopify subscription, access to the relevant property, and access to the Meta pixel or dataset.
Does not import orders from before the connection or predict future customer value.
Profit LTV requires complete order costs. A running profit total also requires costs for earlier orders.
The merchant must create the Meta custom conversion and select it in the ad set.

use_cases.title: Check Shopify Tracking Readiness
use_cases.description: Find missing app, consent, or Meta connection steps before testing the first lifetime value event.

use_cases.title: Pilot a Revenue LTV Ad Set
use_cases.description: Verify the revenue LTV event and choose its custom conversion for one Meta ad set.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Missing Profit LTV
use_cases.description: Check whether missing variant costs, additional costs, or consent prevent a paid test order from producing a profit LTV event.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup Status
prompt_templates.scenario: You want to know whether your Shopify store is ready for LTV bidding.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check setup status for my Shopify property. Tell me what is complete and what I need to do next. Do not change settings.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Test Order
prompt_templates.scenario: You have placed a paid test order with the required consent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether Product Metrics recognized the customer on test order [order ID]. Tell me how to confirm the revenue LTV event in Meta.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Missing Profit
prompt_templates.scenario: Test events show revenue LTV but not profit LTV.
prompt_templates.prompt: For test order [order ID], check what could prevent profit LTV delivery. Separate missing costs, consent settings, and delivery issues. Leave settings unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Single Ad Set Pilot
prompt_templates.scenario: You need to choose between optimizing for lifetime revenue and lifetime profit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare revenue LTV and profit LTV for one Meta ad set. Specify the event and filter, test checks, and what I should review before choosing a ROAS goal.

output_examples.input: The revenue LTV event is missing from the custom conversion selector. What should I check?
output: Verify that your Meta destination points to the intended pixel or dataset.
Place a paid test order for a recognized customer with analytics and ad user data consent.
Confirm that Meta receives the revenue LTV event before creating the custom conversion.

output_examples.input: I can see revenue LTV, but my paid test order has no profit LTV event.
output: Check the Shopify cost per item for every variant on the order.
Verify that payment, shipping, handling, and return costs are configured where applicable.
Place another paid test order after correcting the missing costs.

best_practices: Verify the consent banner before enabling event delivery.
Enter Meta access tokens only in the verified Product Metrics app.
Pilot one ad set and verify that its selected conversion matches the intended LTV event.
anti_patterns: Using the order-profit conversion to optimize for lifetime profit.
Copying the purchase ROAS goal without checking the value sent by the LTV event.
Leaving the test event code configured after validation.

faq.question: Does the skill predict what customers will spend?
faq.answer: No. It uses observed paid orders after tracking starts. It does not import earlier orders or predict future spending.

faq.question: What value does each LTV event send?
faq.answer: The event value is the amount the current order adds. The running total is sent separately when available.

faq.question: What consent does an LTV event require?
faq.answer: The documented setup requires both analytics consent and ad user data consent. Verify that Product Metrics uses the banner the store displays.

faq.question: Why is profit LTV missing when revenue LTV works?
faq.answer: Profit LTV requires complete costs for the order. Check the Shopify variant costs and the applicable additional costs in Product Metrics.

faq.question: Why is the event missing from Meta's selector?
faq.answer: Meta must receive the event before it appears in the selector. Use a paid test order with the required consent, then check Events Manager.

faq.question: Who changes the ad set's optimization event?
faq.answer: The merchant selects the custom conversion in Meta. The assistant can explain the steps and help verify the selection.
